conventions.convention: The sites are Γ = Z^d with d ≥ 1, fixed finite spin dimension q ≥ 1, and max-coordinate metric. Finite regions may be empty; the empty-region algebra is C. Tensor-with-identity inclusions preserve the operator norm.

Interactions are indexed by finite nonempty supports, are self-adjoint, vanish beyond support size M or diameter R, and satisfy κ = sup_x Σ_{Z containing x} ||Φ(Z)|| < ∞. Terms sharing a support are added before taking its norm.

Free-boundary H_Λ includes only interaction supports wholly contained in Λ. With ℏ > 0, α_t^Λ(A) = exp(itH_Λ/ℏ) A exp(-itH_Λ/ℏ), extended by identity on exterior tensor factors. In the energy interpretation, H_Λ and κ have units J, t has units s, and ℏ has units J s.
An increasing finite exhaustion is indexed by n ≥ 1, is nested, and has union Z^d; geometric regularity of its boundaries is not required.

The thermodynamic theorem assumes Countable Choice and the stated finite-matrix C*-identity. Strong continuity means norm continuity of t ↦ α_t(A) for each fixed A, rather than continuity in the operator norm on maps.
The generator is defined by the two-sided norm limit at t = 0, with sign δ(A) = (i/ℏ) Σ_{Z meeting X} [Φ(Z), A] on local observables.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity condition [A1]. For a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction on the specified quasi-local spin algebra, free-boundary dynamics along any increasing finite exhaustion converge in norm on every local observable, uniformly on compact time intervals. The exhaustion-independent limit extends uniquely to a strongly continuous one-parameter group of complex-linear unital *-automorphisms of the completion, with inverse α_{-t}.

For finite nonempty Z ⊂ Z^d, Φ(Z) ∈ A_Z is self-adjoint; there are M ≥ 1, finite R ≥ 0 and κ = sup_x Σ_{Z containing x} ||Φ(Z)|| < ∞ such that Φ(Z) = 0 when |Z| > M or diam∞ Z > R. H_Λ sums only supports contained in Λ, and α_t^Λ(A) = exp(itH_Λ/ℏ) A exp(-itH_Λ/ℏ), with ℏ > 0.
For μ > 0, finite Λ, finite nonempty X ⊆ Λ and Y ⊂ Z^d, A ∈ A_X and B ∈ A_Y embedded in A_{Λ∪Y}, every real t satisfies ||[α_t^Λ(A), B]|| ≤ 2||A||||B|||X| exp((2κM exp(μR)/ℏ)|t| − μ dist∞(X,Y)).

For μ > 0, finite nonempty X ⊆ Λ ⊆ Λ′, A ∈ A_X and real t, ||α_t^{Λ′}(A) − α_t^Λ(A)|| ≤ (2κ|X|||A|||t|/ℏ) exp((2κM exp(μR)/ℏ)|t| + μR) Σ_{y outside Λ} exp(−μ dist∞(X,{y})). The sum is finite and its exterior tail tends to zero along every increasing finite exhaustion, giving compact-time norm Cauchy convergence on local observables.

Under the hypotheses of thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics, the generator defined by the norm difference quotient is closed. Every local A ∈ A_X belongs to its domain and has δ(A) = (i/ℏ) Σ_{Z meeting X} [Φ(Z), A], a finite sum independent of the localization region.

concerns.concern: The Statement covers every local A ∈ A_X, allowing X = ∅ under def-qsm-local-spin-algebras. Proof step 1.1 immediately defines X^{+R} using dist∞(X,{y}), although the interaction definition defines this distance only for nonempty sets. Handle scalar observables separately or first enlarge their localization to a nonempty one, as the dynamics theorem already does. For scalars the asserted generator value is zero, so this is an immediately repairable proof boundary gap.

seams_checked.note: The local-algebra, inclusion and completion interfaces match their uses. Countable Choice and the finite-matrix identity are explicitly retained; draft readiness is distinguished from mathematical acceptance.

The translation-invariant interaction definition specializes the bounded finite-range interaction and preserves the free-boundary Hamiltonian convention. The pressure page does not invoke dynamics to infer equilibrium classification or relaxation.

The KMS definition, Gibbs strip-limit lemma and infinite-spin existence theorem use pointwise norm continuity, compact-real-time local convergence and the finite local generator formula with the same sign and ℏ normalization. They retain the completion hypotheses and assert no global Gibbs density or relaxation.

The algebraic Kubo theorem explicitly carries Countable Choice and the finite-matrix identity, uses the strongly continuous isometric group, and separately assumes state invariance. It does not infer temporal decay or a dc coefficient from finite spatial range.
